detail:
Keys and chains: (1) R2|fnn-owner-stop-service-locked|O:sb-bsd-sockets:socket-shutdown x2 -- fnn-owner-stop-service-locked (owner.lisp:2845) 'locked' = O held (e.g. fnn-owner-commit-complete-locked owner.lisp:4703 -> :2893 listener shutdown, :2902 client shutdown, each in ignore-errors). The comment at owner.lisp:2886-2890 states the design: shutdown (not close) so the accept loop observes STOPPING 'while this mutex is still held'. shutdown(2) does not block on a TCP socket. (2) R2|fnn-socket-shutdown|XCTL:sb-bsd-sockets:socket-shutdown -- fnn-dev-repl-stop (dev-repl.lisp:243): the dev REPL's control-state lock held while shutting its clients/listener; developer tool. (3) R2|fnn-mux-close-wake|M:sb-posix:close -- fnn-mux-close-wake (mux.lisp:1683) closes the loop's two wake pipe fds with fnn-mux-loop-lock held, recording a per-fd receipt before the call (so a failed close is never retried).
Hazard: each leaf is a non-blocking kernel call on a socket or pipe (EIO/EINTR possible on close); the lock exists to order the teardown with the lifecycle flag. Held and reachable, stalls improbable.
fix: Justify by design decision (the stop-service comment already does): declare these three sites as R2 exceptions in the contracts with the shutdown/close rationale, or mark the sockets/pipes non-blocking-leaf class in the checker's leaf classifier if Deputy C prefers. Low priority.
notes: Not changed in lane/lock-owner-class. All three sites (fnn-owner-stop-service-locked socket-shutdown x2, fnn-socket-shutdown under the dev REPL control lock, fnn-mux-close-wake close under fnn-mux-loop-lock) are non-blocking leaf calls whose lock orders the teardown with a lifecycle flag; the item's fix is an R2 exception or leaf classification, which the lane rules allow only as a checker-verified model-gap row and the item text does not call a model gap. Left for Deputy C.

Deputy C2 ruling 2026-10-07: (a) shutdown(2) does not wait (SO_LINGER governs close, not shutdown), so sb-bsd-sockets:socket-shutdown leaves R2's blocking-leaf set as a model correction (contracts nonblocking_leaves, read by compute_blocking and rule_R2; the leaf keeps its socket-error signal class for R7); (b) close(2) of a pipe fd does not block, accepted only with checker-verified provenance (contracts nonblocking_close_sites, verify_pipe_close_sites: every store into the wake slots is NIL or an sb-posix:pipe result, no constructor passes a slot keyword).

Fixed at 96fd09f81 (shutdown) and 56220aa56 (pipe close): keys R2|fnn-owner-stop-service-locked|O:sb-bsd-sockets:socket-shutdown, R2|fnn-socket-shutdown|XCTL:sb-bsd-sockets:socket-shutdown and R2|fnn-mux-close-wake|M:sb-posix:close gone from --check on lane/lock-owner-class, none added. Unit tests: R2NonblockingLeaf, R2PipeClose in tests/test_lock_discipline_check.py.

lock-io-out statement (wake pipe): M stages a :calling receipt before close(2), with CLOSED already set; close runs off M, then M rechecks receipt identity and descriptor identity before clearing the owning slot or retaining a condition as debt. A second closer sees the receipt as already taken, and wake writers see CLOSED, so neither can reuse the staged descriptor. Socket shutdown paths are being traced separately.

lock-io-out statement (service/control sockets): O first installs the monotone STOPPING fence and stages a shutdown receipt with the exact non-sparing sockets and stop hooks. After owner release, one drainer marks that receipt :calling under O, shuts sockets and invokes hooks off O, then checks receipt identity under O and marks it returned. A competing stop sees the existing receipt and cannot take it twice; admission already sees STOPPING. The dev REPL hook similarly snapshots clients/listener while setting its XCTL stopping flag, then shuts them down off XCTL; its sole worker retains close custody, and no new client is admitted after stopping.

lock-io-out result: fnn-mux-close-wake stages under M and closes off M. Owner shutdown uses O to fence and the roster lock to claim/settle its exact wake receipt; fnn-section-envelope, fnn-owner-stop-service and fnn-owner-fault-service drain after O release. fnn-dev-repl-stop claims STOPPING under XCTL, signals off-lock and rechecks its fence under XCTL. Existing shutdown/pipe exceptions already hid these keys on HEAD; no new allowance added. Natives owed: tests/test_native_owner.py, tests/test_native_mux.py, tests/test_native_control.py; developer REPL stop/close overlap and two simultaneous wake-pipe closers need schedules on the image.
scenario: Service stop, dev REPL stop, mux loop shutdown. A close/shutdown that hung would hold the lifecycle lock.

title: Descriptor teardown (socket-shutdown, close) is issued under the lock that guards the lifecycle: stop-service (O), dev-repl-stop (XCTL), mux-close-wake (M)
